def transform(x: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    Supported verbs: jump, walk, run, look
    Directions: left, right
    Modifiers: around (default), opposite
    Quantifiers: once, twice, thrice (default = once)
    The keyword “after” reverses the order of the two (or more) clauses.
    """
    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------
    turn_map = {"left": "I_TURN_LEFT", "right": "I_TURN_RIGHT"}
    verb_map = {"jump": "I_JUMP", "walk": "I_WALK", "run": "I_RUN", "look": "I_LOOK"}
    quant_map = {"once": 1, "twice": 2, "thrice": 3}

    def expand_clause(tokens):
        """tokens = list of words for a single clause, return list of actions."""
        # quantifier (optional, at the end)
        if tokens[-1] in quant_map:
            count = quant_map[tokens.pop()]          # remove quantifier
        else:
            count = 1

        # direction is always the last remaining token
        direction = tokens.pop()                    # left / right
        turn = turn_map[direction]

        # modifier (optional) – token before direction
        if tokens and tokens[-1] in {"around", "opposite"}:
            modifier = tokens.pop()
        else:
            modifier = "around"                     # default

        # verb is the first (and only) remaining token
        verb = tokens[0]
        action = verb_map[verb]

        # build one repetition
        if modifier == "around":
            unit = [turn, action]
        else:  # opposite → two turns of the same direction
            unit = [turn, turn, action]

        # repeat as required
        return unit * count

    # ----- main parsing ---------------------------------------------
    # split on the keyword “after”; the order of execution is reversed
    parts = [p.strip() for p in x.split(" after ")]
    # process each part and concatenate in reverse order
    result = []
    for part in reversed(parts):
        tokens = part.split()
        result.extend(expand_clause(tokens))

    return " ".join(result)

def transform(x: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    Supported verbs: jump, walk, run, look
    Directions: left, right
    Modifiers: around (default), opposite
    Quantifiers: once, twice, thrice (default = once)
    The keyword “after” reverses the order of the two (or more) clauses.
    """
    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------
    turn_map = {"left": "I_TURN_LEFT", "right": "I_TURN_RIGHT"}
    verb_map = {"jump": "I_JUMP", "walk": "I_WALK", "run": "I_RUN", "look": "I_LOOK"}
    quant_map = {"once": 1, "twice": 2, "thrice": 3}

    def expand_clause(tokens):
        """tokens = list of words for a single clause, return list of actions."""
        # quantifier (optional, at the end)
        if tokens[-1] in quant_map:
            count = quant_map[tokens.pop()]          # remove quantifier
        else:
            count = 1

        # direction is always the last remaining token
        direction = tokens.pop()                    # left / right
        turn = turn_map[direction]

        # modifier (optional) – token before direction
        if tokens and tokens[-1] in {"around", "opposite"}:
            modifier = tokens.pop()
        else:
            modifier = "around"                     # default

        # verb is the first (and only) remaining token
        verb = tokens[0]
        action = verb_map[verb]

        # build one repetition
        if modifier == "around":
            unit = [turn, action]
        else:  # opposite → two turns of the same direction
            unit = [turn, turn, action]

        # repeat as required
        return unit * count

    # ----- main parsing ---------------------------------------------
    # split on the keyword “after”; the order of execution is reversed
    parts = [p.strip() for p in x.split(" after ")]
    # process each part and concatenate in reverse order
    result = []
    for part in reversed(parts):
        tokens = part.split()
        result.extend(expand_clause(tokens))

    return " ".join(result)

def transform(x: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    Supported verbs: jump, walk, run, look
    Directions: left, right
    Modifiers: around (default), opposite
    Quantifiers: once, twice, thrice (default = once)
    The keyword “after” reverses the order of the two (or more) clauses.
    """
    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------
    turn_map = {"left": "I_TURN_LEFT", "right": "I_TURN_RIGHT"}
    verb_map = {"jump": "I_JUMP", "walk": "I_WALK", "run": "I_RUN", "look": "I_LOOK"}
    quant_map = {"once": 1, "twice": 2, "thrice": 3}

    def expand_clause(tokens):
        """tokens = list of words for a single clause, return list of actions."""
        # quantifier (optional, at the end)
        if tokens[-1] in quant_map:
            count = quant_map[tokens.pop()]          # remove quantifier
        else:
            count = 1

        # direction is always the last remaining token
        direction = tokens.pop()                    # left / right
        turn = turn_map[direction]

        # modifier (optional) – token before direction
        if tokens and tokens[-1] in {"around", "opposite"}:
            modifier = tokens.pop()
        else:
            modifier = "around"                     # default

        # verb is the first (and only) remaining token
        verb = tokens[0]
        action = verb_map[verb]

        # build one repetition
        if modifier == "around":
            unit = [turn, action]
        else:  # opposite → two turns of the same direction
            unit = [turn, turn, action]

        # repeat as required
        return unit * count

    # ----- main parsing ---------------------------------------------
    # split on the keyword “after”; the order of execution is reversed
    parts = [p.strip() for p in x.split(" after ")]
    # process each part and concatenate in reverse order
    result = []
    for part in reversed(parts):
        tokens = part.split()
        result.extend(expand_clause(tokens))

    return " ".join(result)

        "six": 6,
        "seven": 7,
        "eight": 8,

                seq.append(f"I_{action.upper()}")
        return seq

def transform(command: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    Supported verbs: jump, walk, run, look, turn.
    Modifiers:
        left / right                – one turn in that direction before the verb
        opposite left / opposite right – two turns in that direction before the verb
        around left / around right      – two turns in that direction before the verb
    Repetition:
        twice   – repeat the whole unit twice
        thrice  – repeat the whole unit three times
    Composition:
        X and Y   – execute X then Y
        X after Y – execute Y then X
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Helper tables
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    VERBS = {"jump", "walk", "run", "look", "turn"}
    DIR_TOK = {"left", "right"}
    COUNT_TOK = {"twice": 2, "thrice": 3}
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Tokeniser
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    tokens = command.strip().split()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Parsing utilities
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def parse_atomic(tok_list):
        """Parse a single verb phrase (no 'and' / 'after')."""
        i = 0
        verb = tok_list[i]
        i += 1
        # collect direction information
        turn_cnt = 0          # how many turns before the verb
        turn_dir = None
        while i < len(tok_list):
            if tok_list[i] in DIR_TOK:
                turn_dir = tok_list[i].upper()
                turn_cnt = 1
                i += 1
            elif tok_list[i] == "opposite":
                # next token must be a direction
                if i + 1 < len(tok_list) and tok_list[i + 1] in DIR_TOK:
                    turn_dir = tok_list[i + 1].upper()
                    turn_cnt = 2
                    i += 2
                else:
                    raise ValueError("bad opposite")
            elif tok_list[i] == "around":
                # next token must be a direction
                if i + 1 < len(tok_list) and tok_list[i + 1] in DIR_TOK:
                    turn_dir = tok_list[i + 1].upper()
                    turn_cnt = 2
                    i += 2
                else:
                    raise ValueError("bad around")
            else:
                break

        # repetition count
        repeat = 1
        if i < len(tok_list) and tok_list[i] in COUNT_TOK:
            repeat = COUNT_TOK[tok_list[i]]
            i += 1

        # Build the primitive action list for one repetition
        unit = []
        if verb == "turn":
            # turn verb itself does not emit a separate I_TURN action;
            # the direction handling already produced the needed turns.
            if turn_dir:
                unit.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_cnt)
        else:
            if turn_dir:
                unit.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_cnt)
            unit.append(f"I_{verb.upper()}")

        return unit * repeat

    def parse_sequence(tok_list):
        """Parse a sequence without top‑level 'after' (handles 'and')."""
        # split on 'and'
        parts = []
        cur = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(tok_list):
            if tok_list[i] == "and":
                parts.append(cur)
                cur = []
                i += 1
            else:
                cur.append(tok_list[i])
                i += 1
        parts.append(cur)

        actions = []
        for part in parts:
            actions.extend(parse_atomic(part))
        return actions

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Top‑level handling of 'after'
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    if "after" in tokens:
        idx = tokens.index("after")
        left = tokens[:idx]          # X
        right = tokens[idx + 1 :]    # Y
        # Y first, then X
        actions = parse_sequence(right) + parse_sequence(left)
    else:
        actions = parse_sequence(tokens)

    return " ".join(actions)

def transform(command: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    Supported verbs: jump, walk, run, look, turn.
    Modifiers:
        left / right                – one turn in that direction before the verb
        opposite left / opposite right – two turns in that direction before the verb
        around left / around right      – two turns in that direction before the verb
    Repetition:
        twice   – repeat the whole unit twice
        thrice  – repeat the whole unit three times
    Composition:
        X and Y   – execute X then Y
        X after Y – execute Y then X
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Helper tables
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    VERBS = {"jump", "walk", "run", "look", "turn"}
    DIR_TOK = {"left", "right"}
    COUNT_TOK = {"twice": 2, "thrice": 3}
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Tokeniser
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    tokens = command.strip().split()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Parsing utilities
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def parse_atomic(tok_list):
        """Parse a single verb phrase (no 'and' / 'after')."""
        i = 0
        verb = tok_list[i]
        i += 1
        # collect direction information
        turn_cnt = 0          # how many turns before the verb
        turn_dir = None
        while i < len(tok_list):
            if tok_list[i] in DIR_TOK:
                turn_dir = tok_list[i].upper()
                turn_cnt = 1
                i += 1
            elif tok_list[i] == "opposite":
                # next token must be a direction
                if i + 1 < len(tok_list) and tok_list[i + 1] in DIR_TOK:
                    turn_dir = tok_list[i + 1].upper()
                    turn_cnt = 2
                    i += 2
                else:
                    raise ValueError("bad opposite")
            elif tok_list[i] == "around":
                # next token must be a direction
                if i + 1 < len(tok_list) and tok_list[i + 1] in DIR_TOK:
                    turn_dir = tok_list[i + 1].upper()
                    turn_cnt = 2
                    i += 2
                else:
                    raise ValueError("bad around")
            else:
                break

        # repetition count
        repeat = 1
        if i < len(tok_list) and tok_list[i] in COUNT_TOK:
            repeat = COUNT_TOK[tok_list[i]]
            i += 1

        # Build the primitive action list for one repetition
        unit = []
        if verb == "turn":
            # turn verb itself does not emit a separate I_TURN action;
            # the direction handling already produced the needed turns.
            if turn_dir:
                unit.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_cnt)
        else:
            if turn_dir:
                unit.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_cnt)
            unit.append(f"I_{verb.upper()}")

        return unit * repeat

    def parse_sequence(tok_list):
        """Parse a sequence without top‑level 'after' (handles 'and')."""
        # split on 'and'
        parts = []
        cur = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(tok_list):
            if tok_list[i] == "and":
                parts.append(cur)
                cur = []
                i += 1
            else:
                cur.append(tok_list[i])
                i += 1
        parts.append(cur)

        actions = []
        for part in parts:
            actions.extend(parse_atomic(part))
        return actions

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Top‑level handling of 'after'
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    if "after" in tokens:
        idx = tokens.index("after")
        left = tokens[:idx]          # X
        right = tokens[idx + 1 :]    # Y
        # Y first, then X
        actions = parse_sequence(right) + parse_sequence(left)
    else:
        actions = parse_sequence(tokens)

    return " ".join(actions)

def transform(command: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    Supported verbs: jump, walk, run, look, turn.
    Modifiers:
        left / right                – one turn in that direction before the verb
        opposite left / opposite right – two turns in that direction before the verb
        around left / around right      – two turns in that direction before the verb
    Repetition:
        twice   – repeat the whole unit twice
        thrice  – repeat the whole unit three times
    Composition:
        X and Y   – execute X then Y
        X after Y – execute Y then X
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Helper tables
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    VERBS = {"jump", "walk", "run", "look", "turn"}
    DIR_TOK = {"left", "right"}
    COUNT_TOK = {"twice": 2, "thrice": 3}
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Tokeniser
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    tokens = command.strip().split()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Parsing utilities
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def parse_atomic(tok_list):
        """Parse a single verb phrase (no 'and' / 'after')."""
        i = 0
        verb = tok_list[i]
        i += 1
        # collect direction information
        turn_cnt = 0          # how many turns before the verb
        turn_dir = None
        while i < len(tok_list):
            if tok_list[i] in DIR_TOK:
                turn_dir = tok_list[i].upper()
                turn_cnt = 1
                i += 1
            elif tok_list[i] == "opposite":
                # next token must be a direction
                if i + 1 < len(tok_list) and tok_list[i + 1] in DIR_TOK:
                    turn_dir = tok_list[i + 1].upper()

                if i + 1 < len(tok_list) and tok_list[i + 1] in DIR_TOK:

                    turn_cnt = 2

        # repetition count
        repeat = 1
        if i < len(tok_list) and tok_list[i] in COUNT_TOK:
            repeat = COUNT_TOK[tok_list[i]]
            i += 1

        # Build the primitive action list for one repetition
        unit = []
        if verb == "turn":
            # turn verb itself does not emit a separate I_TURN action;
            # the direction handling already produced the needed turns.
            if turn_dir:
                unit.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_cnt)
        else:
            if turn_dir:
                unit.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_cnt)
            unit.append(f"I_{verb.upper()}")

        return unit * repeat

    def parse_sequence(tok_list):
        """Parse a sequence without top‑level 'after' (handles 'and')."""

        parts = []
        cur = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(tok_list):
            if tok_list[i] == "and":

                cur = []
                i += 1
            else:
                cur.append(tok_list[i])

        parts.append(cur)

        actions = []
        for part in parts:
            actions.extend(parse_atomic(part))
        return actions

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Top‑level handling of 'after'
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    if "after" in tokens:

        left = tokens[:idx]          # X
        right = tokens[idx + 1 :]    # Y
        # Y first, then X
        actions = parse_sequence(right) + parse_sequence(left)
    else:
        actions = parse_sequence(tokens)

    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    The interpreter follows the rules inferred from the examples:

    * Verbs: jump, walk, run, look, turn.
    * Direction modifiers (optional, may consist of one or two words):
        - left                → one left turn
        - right               → one right turn
        - around left/right   → one left/right turn
        - opposite left/right → two left/right turns
    * Count modifiers (optional, placed at the end of a clause):
        - twice   → 2 repetitions
        - thrice  → 3 repetitions
      If no explicit count is given:
        – for verbs **with** an “around” modifier the default repetition is 4,
        – otherwise the default repetition is 1.
    * “and” concatenates clauses left‑to‑right.
    * “after” swaps the order:  A after B  →  B then A.
    * For the verb **turn**, the direction turns *are* the action;
      for all other verbs the direction turns precede the verb’s primitive action.
    """
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # helpers
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    turn_map = {
        "left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "around left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "around right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "opposite left": ["I_TURN_LEFT", "I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "opposite right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT", "I_TURN_RIGHT"],
    }

    verb_action = {
        "jump": "I_JUMP",
        "walk": "I_WALK",
        "run": "I_RUN",
        "look": "I_LOOK",
        "turn": None,          # turn has no extra primitive; its action is the turn(s) themselves
    }

    count_word = {"twice": 2, "thrice": 3}

    def get_turns(dir_phrase: str):
        """Return the list of turn tokens for a direction phrase."""
        return turn_map.get(dir_phrase, [])

    def parse_clause(clause: str):
        """Parse a single clause (no 'and' or 'after') into a list of actions."""
        tokens = clause.split()
        # ----- count -----
        cnt = 1
        if tokens and tokens[-1] in count_word:
            cnt = count_word[tokens.pop()]          # remove the count word
        # ----- verb -----
        verb = tokens[0]
        # ----- direction phrase -----
        dir_phrase = " ".join(tokens[1:])            # may be empty
        turns = get_turns(dir_phrase)

        # ----- base repetition (for 'around' without explicit count) -----
        base_rep = 4 if ("around" in dir_phrase and verb != "turn") else 1
        total_rep = base_rep * cnt

        # ----- build actions -----
        actions = []
        if verb == "turn":
            # turn verb: the direction turns *are* the action
            actions = turns * total_rep
        else:
            primitive = verb_action[verb]
            seq = turns + [primitive]
            actions = seq * total_rep
        return actions

    def parse_part(part: str):
        """Parse a part that may contain several clauses joined by 'and'."""
        clauses = [c.strip() for c in part.split(" and ")]
        out = []
        for cl in clauses:
            out.extend(parse_clause(cl))
        return out

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # main parsing (handle 'after')
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    x = x.strip()
    if " after " in x:
        left, right = x.split(" after ", 1)   # left = before 'after', right = after
        actions = parse_part(right) + parse_part(left)
    else:
        actions = parse_part(x)

    return " ".join(actions)

def transform(x: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    The interpreter follows the rules inferred from the examples:

    * Verbs: jump, walk, run, look, turn.
    * Direction modifiers (optional, may consist of one or two words):
        - left                → one left turn
        - right               → one right turn
        - around left/right   → one left/right turn
        - opposite left/right → two left/right turns
    * Count modifiers (optional, placed at the end of a clause):
        - twice   → 2 repetitions
        - thrice  → 3 repetitions
      If no explicit count is given:
        – for verbs **with** an “around” modifier the default repetition is 4,
        – otherwise the default repetition is 1.
    * “and” concatenates clauses left‑to‑right.
    * “after” swaps the order:  A after B  →  B then A.
    * For the verb **turn**, the direction turns *are* the action;
      for all other verbs the direction turns precede the verb’s primitive action.
    """
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # helpers
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    turn_map = {
        "left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "around left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "around right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "opposite left": ["I_TURN_LEFT", "I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "opposite right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT", "I_TURN_RIGHT"],
    }

    verb_action = {
        "jump": "I_JUMP",
        "walk": "I_WALK",
        "run": "I_RUN",
        "look": "I_LOOK",
        "turn": None,          # turn has no extra primitive; its action is the turn(s) themselves
    }

    count_word = {"twice": 2, "thrice": 3}

    def get_turns(dir_phrase: str):
        """Return the list of turn tokens for a direction phrase."""
        return turn_map.get(dir_phrase, [])

    def parse_clause(clause: str):
        """Parse a single clause (no 'and' or 'after') into a list of actions."""
        tokens = clause.split()
        # ----- count -----
        cnt = 1
        if tokens and tokens[-1] in count_word:
            cnt = count_word[tokens.pop()]          # remove the count word
        # ----- verb -----
        verb = tokens[0]
        # ----- direction phrase -----
        dir_phrase = " ".join(tokens[1:])            # may be empty
        turns = get_turns(dir_phrase)

        # ----- base repetition (for 'around' without explicit count) -----
        base_rep = 4 if ("around" in dir_phrase and verb != "turn") else 1
        total_rep = base_rep * cnt

        # ----- build actions -----
        actions = []
        if verb == "turn":
            # turn verb: the direction turns *are* the action
            actions = turns * total_rep
        else:
            primitive = verb_action[verb]
            seq = turns + [primitive]
            actions = seq * total_rep
        return actions

    def parse_part(part: str):
        """Parse a part that may contain several clauses joined by 'and'."""
        clauses = [c.strip() for c in part.split(" and ")]
        out = []
        for cl in clauses:
            out.extend(parse_clause(cl))
        return out

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # main parsing (handle 'after')
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    x = x.strip()
    if " after " in x:
        left, right = x.split(" after ", 1)   # left = before 'after', right = after
        actions = parse_part(right) + parse_part(left)
    else:
        actions = parse_part(x)

    return " ".join(actions)

def transform(x: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    The interpreter follows the rules inferred from the examples:

    * Verbs: jump, walk, run, look, turn.
    * Direction modifiers (optional, may consist of one or two words):
        - left                → one left turn
        - right               → one right turn
        - around left/right   → one left/right turn
        - opposite left/right → two left/right turns
    * Count modifiers (optional, placed at the end of a clause):
        - twice   → 2 repetitions
        - thrice  → 3 repetitions
      If no explicit count is given:
        – for verbs **with** an “around” modifier the default repetition is 4,
        – otherwise the default repetition is 1.
    * “and” concatenates clauses left‑to‑right.
    * “after” swaps the order:  A after B  →  B then A.
    * For the verb **turn**, the direction turns *are* the action;
      for all other verbs the direction turns precede the verb’s primitive action.
    """
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # helpers
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    turn_map = {
        "left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "around left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "around right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "opposite left": ["I_TURN_LEFT", "I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "opposite right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT", "I_TURN_RIGHT"],
    }

    verb_action = {
        "jump": "I_JUMP",
        "walk": "I_WALK",
        "run": "I_RUN",
        "look": "I_LOOK",
        "turn": None,          # turn has no extra primitive; its action is the turn(s) themselves
    }

    count_word = {"twice": 2, "thrice": 3}

    def get_turns(dir_phrase: str):
        """Return the list of turn tokens for a direction phrase."""
        return turn_map.get(dir_phrase, [])

    def parse_clause(clause: str):
        """Parse a single clause (no 'and' or 'after') into a list of actions."""
        tokens = clause.split()
        # ----- count -----
        cnt = 1
        if tokens and tokens[-1] in count_word:
            cnt = count_word[tokens.pop()]          # remove the count word
        # ----- verb -----
        verb = tokens[0]
        # ----- direction phrase -----
        dir_phrase = " ".join(tokens[1:])            # may be empty
        turns = get_turns(dir_phrase)

        # ----- base repetition (for 'around' without explicit count) -----
        base_rep = 4 if ("around" in dir_phrase and verb != "turn") else 1
        total_rep = base_rep * cnt

        # ----- build actions -----
        actions = []
        if verb == "turn":
            # turn verb: the direction turns *are* the action
            actions = turns * total_rep
        else:
            primitive = verb_action[verb]
            seq = turns + [primitive]
            actions = seq * total_rep
        return actions

    def parse_part(part: str):
        """Parse a part that may contain several clauses joined by 'and'."""
        clauses = [c.strip() for c in part.split(" and ")]
        out = []
        for cl in clauses:
            out.extend(parse_clause(cl))
        return out

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # main parsing (handle 'after')
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    x = x.strip()
    if " after " in x:
        left, right = x.split(" after ", 1)   # left = before 'after', right = after
        actions = parse_part(right) + parse_part(left)
    else:
        actions = parse_part(x)

    return " ".join(actions)

    """
    Convert a SCAN command string into a space‑separated sequence of
    primitive actions (I_TURN_LEFT, I_TURN_RIGHT, I_JUMP, I_WALK,
    I_RUN, I_LOOK).

    Grammar (simplified):
        expr   ::= expr " after " expr
                 | expr " and "   expr
                 | simple
        simple ::= verb [modifier] [direction] [count]
        verb   ::= "jump" | "walk" | "run" | "look" | "turn"
        modifier ::= "around" | "opposite"
        direction ::= "left" | "right"
        count ::= "twice" | "thrice"

    Semantics:
        * “around D”   – turn D once before the primitive action.
        * “opposite D” – turn D twice (180°) before the primitive action.
        * “turn D”     – primitive turn in direction D.
        * “turn around D” – turn D, then turn D again.
        * “turn opposite D” – turn D twice (no extra turn).
        * Count repeats the whole (modifier+direction+verb) block.
        * “A and B”    – execute A then B.
        * “A after B”  – execute B then A.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def repeat(seq, n):
        return seq * n

    def parse_simple(tokens):
        """Parse a token list that represents a single command."""
        verb = tokens[0]
        i = 1
        modifier = None
        direction = None
        count = 1

        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in ("around", "opposite"):
            modifier = tokens[i]
            i += 1

        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in ("left", "right"):

            i += 1

        prim = {
            "jump": "I_JUMP",
            "walk": "I_WALK",
            "run":  "I_RUN",
            "look": "I_LOOK",
        }[verb] if verb != "turn" else None

            # direction is mandatory for turn
            dir_tok = direction.upper()
            if modifier == "around":
                base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}"]
            elif modifier == "opposite":

            else:
                base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}"]
        else:

                if modifier == "around":

                elif modifier == "opposite":
                    base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", prim]
                else:  # direction without explicit modifier – treat like “around”
                    base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", prim]
            else:
                base = [prim]

        return repeat(base, count)

            return parse_expr(left) + parse_expr(right)
        # simple command
        tokens = s.split()
        return parse_simple(tokens)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # main entry
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    actions = parse_expr(x.lower())
    return " ".join(actions)

    """
    Convert a SCAN command string into a space‑separated sequence of
    primitive actions (I_TURN_LEFT, I_TURN_RIGHT, I_JUMP, I_WALK,

    Grammar (simplified):
        expr   ::= expr " after " expr
                 | expr " and "   expr
                 | simple
        simple ::= verb [modifier] [direction] [count]
        verb   ::= "jump" | "walk" | "run" | "look" | "turn"
        modifier ::= "around" | "opposite"
        direction ::= "left" | "right"
        count ::= "twice" | "thrice"

    Semantics:
        * “around D”   – turn D once before the primitive action.
        * “opposite D” – turn D twice (180°) before the primitive action.
        * “turn D”     – primitive turn in direction D.
        * “turn around D” – turn D, then turn D again.
        * “turn opposite D” – turn D twice (no extra turn).
        * Count repeats the whole (modifier+direction+verb) block.
        * “A and B”    – execute A then B.
        * “A after B”  – execute B then A.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def repeat(seq, n):
        return seq * n

    def parse_simple(tokens):
        """Parse a token list that represents a single command."""
        verb = tokens[0]
        i = 1
        modifier = None
        direction = None
        count = 1

        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in ("around", "opposite"):
            modifier = tokens[i]
            i += 1

        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in ("left", "right"):
            direction = tokens[i]
            i += 1

        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in ("twice", "thrice"):
            count = 2 if tokens[i] == "twice" else 3
            i += 1

        # primitive action for the verb
        prim = {
            "jump": "I_JUMP",
            "walk": "I_WALK",
            "run":  "I_RUN",
            "look": "I_LOOK",
        }[verb] if verb != "turn" else None

        # build the base sequence (without repetition)
        if verb == "turn":
            # direction is mandatory for turn
            dir_tok = direction.upper()
            if modifier == "around":
                base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}"]

            else:

        else:

                    base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", prim]
                elif modifier == "opposite":
                    base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", prim]
                else:  # direction without explicit modifier – treat like “around”
                    base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", prim]
            else:
                base = [prim]

        return repeat(base, count)

    def parse_expr(s):
        """Recursive descent for the whole expression."""
        s = s.strip()
        # “after” has lower precedence than “and”
        if " after " in s:
            left, right = s.split(" after ", 1)
            return parse_expr(right) + parse_expr(left)
        if " and " in s:
            left, right = s.split(" and ", 1)
            return parse_expr(left) + parse_expr(right)
        # simple command
        tokens = s.split()
        return parse_simple(tokens)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # main entry
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    actions = parse_expr(x.lower())
    return " ".join(actions)

def transform(x: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN command string into a space‑separated sequence of
    primitive actions (I_TURN_LEFT, I_TURN_RIGHT, I_JUMP, I_WALK,
    I_RUN, I_LOOK).

    Grammar (simplified):
        expr   ::= expr " after " expr
                 | expr " and "   expr
                 | simple
        simple ::= verb [modifier] [direction] [count]
        verb   ::= "jump" | "walk" | "run" | "look" | "turn"
        modifier ::= "around" | "opposite"
        direction ::= "left" | "right"
        count ::= "twice" | "thrice"

    Semantics:
        * “around D”   – turn D once before the primitive action.
        * “opposite D” – turn D twice (180°) before the primitive action.
        * “turn D”     – primitive turn in direction D.
        * “turn around D” – turn D, then turn D again.
        * “turn opposite D” – turn D twice (no extra turn).
        * Count repeats the whole (modifier+direction+verb) block.
        * “A and B”    – execute A then B.
        * “A after B”  – execute B then A.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def repeat(seq, n):
        return seq * n

    def parse_simple(tokens):
        """Parse a token list that represents a single command."""
        verb = tokens[0]
        i = 1
        modifier = None
        direction = None
        count = 1

        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in ("around", "opposite"):
            modifier = tokens[i]
            i += 1

        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in ("left", "right"):
            direction = tokens[i]
            i += 1

        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in ("twice", "thrice"):
            count = 2 if tokens[i] == "twice" else 3
            i += 1

        # primitive action for the verb
        prim = {
            "jump": "I_JUMP",
            "walk": "I_WALK",
            "run":  "I_RUN",
            "look": "I_LOOK",
        }[verb] if verb != "turn" else None

        # build the base sequence (without repetition)
        if verb == "turn":
            # direction is mandatory for turn
            dir_tok = direction.upper()
            if modifier == "around":
                base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}"]
            elif modifier == "opposite":
                base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}"]
            else:
                base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}"]
        else:
            if direction:
                dir_tok = direction.upper()
                if modifier == "around":
                    base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", prim]
                elif modifier == "opposite":
                    base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", prim]
                else:  # direction without explicit modifier – treat like “around”
                    base = [f"I_TURN_{dir_tok}", prim]
            else:
                base = [prim]

        return repeat(base, count)

    def parse_expr(s):
        """Recursive descent for the whole expression."""
        s = s.strip()
        # “after” has lower precedence than “and”
        if " after " in s:
            left, right = s.split(" after ", 1)
            return parse_expr(right) + parse_expr(left)
        if " and " in s:
            left, right = s.split(" and ", 1)
            return parse_expr(left) + parse_expr(right)
        # simple command
        tokens = s.split()
        return parse_simple(tokens)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # main entry
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    actions = parse_expr(x.lower())
    return " ".join(actions)

    if " after " in s:
        left, right = s.split(" after ", 1)
        return parse(right) + parse(left)
    # handle and
    parts = s.split(" and ")
    seq = []
    for part in parts:
        seq += parse_phrase(part)
    return seq

def parse_phrase(p):
    tokens = p.split()
    repeat = 1
    if tokens[-1] in ("twice","thrice"):
        repeat = 2 if tokens[-1]=="twice" else 3
        tokens = tokens[:-1]
    verb = tokens[0]
    direction = " ".join(tokens[1:])  # may be empty
    # map direction to turn list
    turn_map = {

        "right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "opposite left": ["I_TURN_LEFT","I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "opposite right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT","I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "around left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "around right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "": []
    }
    pre_turns = turn_map.get(direction, [])
    seq = []
    if verb == "turn":

        seq = base * repeat

            if direction.startswith("around") and i != repeat-1:

    return seq

def transform(x: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN command string into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    """
    # mapping from primitive verbs to their action codes
    ACT = {"jump": "I_JUMP", "walk": "I_WALK", "run": "I_RUN", "look": "I_LOOK"}

    # turn sequences for the various direction modifiers
    TURN_SINGLE = {
        "left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "opposite left": ["I_TURN_LEFT", "I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "opposite right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT", "I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "around left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],   # for verbs – the post‑turn is handled by repetition
        "around right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "": [],
    }

    def parse_phrase(p: str) -> list:
        """Parse a single phrase (no 'and' / 'after') into a list of actions."""
        tokens = p.strip().split()
        # ----- repetition factor (twice / thrice) -----
        rep_factor = 1
        if tokens and tokens[-1] in ("twice", "thrice"):
            rep_factor = 2 if tokens[-1] == "twice" else 3
            tokens = tokens[:-1]

        verb = tokens[0]
        direction = " ".join(tokens[1:])  # may be empty

        # ----- verbs that are pure turns -----
        if verb == "turn":
            # base turn list for one execution of the phrase
            if direction.startswith("around"):
                base = ["I_TURN_LEFT"] * 4 if "left" in direction else ["I_TURN_RIGHT"] * 4
            else:
                base = TURN_SINGLE.get(direction, [])
            return base * rep_factor

        # ----- verbs that are actions (jump, walk, run, look) -----
        act = ACT[verb]

        # determine how many times the core pattern must be repeated
        # an 'around' modifier expands to four repetitions when no explicit count is given
        base_repeat = 4 if direction.startswith("around") else 1
        total_repeat = base_repeat * rep_factor

        pre_turns = TURN_SINGLE.get(direction, [])

        seq = []
        for i in range(total_repeat):
            seq.extend(pre_turns)          # turn(s) before the action
            seq.append(act)                # the primitive action
            # for an 'around' direction we need a turn after the action,
            # but that turn is also the pre‑turn of the next iteration,
            # so we add it only when another iteration follows.
            if direction.startswith("around") and i != total_repeat - 1:
                seq.extend(pre_turns)
        return seq

    def parse(s: str) -> list:
        """Recursively handle 'after' and 'and' operators."""
        s = s.strip()
        # 'after' has the lowest precedence: X after Y  →  Y then X
        if " after " in s:
            left, right = s.split(" after ", 1)
            return parse(right) + parse(left)

        # 'and' concatenates in the given order
        parts = s.split(" and ")
        result = []
        for part in parts:
            result.extend(parse_phrase(part))
        return result

    return " ".join(parse(x))

def transform(x: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN command string into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    """
    # mapping from primitive verbs to their action codes
    ACT = {"jump": "I_JUMP", "walk": "I_WALK", "run": "I_RUN", "look": "I_LOOK"}

    # turn sequences for the various direction modifiers
    TURN_SINGLE = {
        "left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "opposite left": ["I_TURN_LEFT", "I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "opposite right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT", "I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "around left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],   # for verbs – the post‑turn is handled by repetition
        "around right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "": [],
    }

    def parse_phrase(p: str) -> list:
        """Parse a single phrase (no 'and' / 'after') into a list of actions."""
        tokens = p.strip().split()
        # ----- repetition factor (twice / thrice) -----
        rep_factor = 1
        if tokens and tokens[-1] in ("twice", "thrice"):
            rep_factor = 2 if tokens[-1] == "twice" else 3
            tokens = tokens[:-1]

        verb = tokens[0]
        direction = " ".join(tokens[1:])  # may be empty

        # ----- verbs that are pure turns -----
        if verb == "turn":
            # base turn list for one execution of the phrase
            if direction.startswith("around"):
                base = ["I_TURN_LEFT"] * 4 if "left" in direction else ["I_TURN_RIGHT"] * 4
            else:
                base = TURN_SINGLE.get(direction, [])
            return base * rep_factor

        # ----- verbs that are actions (jump, walk, run, look) -----
        act = ACT[verb]

        # determine how many times the core pattern must be repeated
        # an 'around' modifier expands to four repetitions when no explicit count is given
        base_repeat = 4 if direction.startswith("around") else 1
        total_repeat = base_repeat * rep_factor

        pre_turns = TURN_SINGLE.get(direction, [])

        seq = []
        for i in range(total_repeat):
            seq.extend(pre_turns)          # turn(s) before the action
            seq.append(act)                # the primitive action
            # for an 'around' direction we need a turn after the action,
            # but that turn is also the pre‑turn of the next iteration,
            # so we add it only when another iteration follows.
            if direction.startswith("around") and i != total_repeat - 1:
                seq.extend(pre_turns)
        return seq

    def parse(s: str) -> list:
        """Recursively handle 'after' and 'and' operators."""
        s = s.strip()
        # 'after' has the lowest precedence: X after Y  →  Y then X
        if " after " in s:
            left, right = s.split(" after ", 1)
            return parse(right) + parse(left)

        # 'and' concatenates in the given order
        parts = s.split(" and ")
        result = []
        for part in parts:
            result.extend(parse_phrase(part))
        return result

    return " ".join(parse(x))

def parse(s):
    s = s.strip()
    # handle after
    if " after " in s:
        left, right = s.split(" after ", 1)
        return parse(right) + parse(left)
    # handle and
    parts = s.split(" and ")
    seq = []
    for part in parts:
        seq += parse_phrase(part)
    return seq

def parse_phrase(p):
    tokens = p.split()
    repeat = 1
    if tokens[-1] in ("twice","thrice"):
        repeat = 2 if tokens[-1]=="twice" else 3
        tokens = tokens[:-1]
    verb = tokens[0]
    direction = " ".join(tokens[1:])  # may be empty
    # map direction to turn list
    turn_map = {
        "left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "opposite left": ["I_TURN_LEFT","I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "opposite right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT","I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "around left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "around right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "": []
    }
    pre_turns = turn_map.get(direction, [])
    seq = []
    if verb == "turn":
        # base turns count
        base = pre_turns
        seq = base * repeat
    else:
        # action token
        act = {"jump":"I_JUMP","walk":"I_WALK","run":"I_RUN","look":"I_LOOK"}[verb]
        for i in range(repeat):
            seq.extend(pre_turns)
            seq.append(act)
            # for around, add post turn except last iteration
            if direction.startswith("around") and i != repeat-1:
                seq.extend(pre_turns)
    return seq

def transform(x: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert a SCAN command string into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    """
    # mapping from primitive verbs to their action codes
    ACT = {"jump": "I_JUMP", "walk": "I_WALK", "run": "I_RUN", "look": "I_LOOK"}

    # turn sequences for the various direction modifiers
    TURN_SINGLE = {
        "left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "opposite left": ["I_TURN_LEFT", "I_TURN_LEFT"],
        "opposite right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT", "I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "around left": ["I_TURN_LEFT"],   # for verbs – the post‑turn is handled by repetition
        "around right": ["I_TURN_RIGHT"],
        "": [],
    }

    def parse_phrase(p: str) -> list:
        """Parse a single phrase (no 'and' / 'after') into a list of actions."""
        tokens = p.strip().split()
        # ----- repetition factor (twice / thrice) -----
        rep_factor = 1
        if tokens and tokens[-1] in ("twice", "thrice"):
            rep_factor = 2 if tokens[-1] == "twice" else 3
            tokens = tokens[:-1]

        verb = tokens[0]
        direction = " ".join(tokens[1:])  # may be empty

        # ----- verbs that are pure turns -----
        if verb == "turn":
            # base turn list for one execution of the phrase
            if direction.startswith("around"):
                base = ["I_TURN_LEFT"] * 4 if "left" in direction else ["I_TURN_RIGHT"] * 4
            else:
                base = TURN_SINGLE.get(direction, [])
            return base * rep_factor

        # ----- verbs that are actions (jump, walk, run, look) -----
        act = ACT[verb]

        # determine how many times the core pattern must be repeated
        # an 'around' modifier expands to four repetitions when no explicit count is given
        base_repeat = 4 if direction.startswith("around") else 1
        total_repeat = base_repeat * rep_factor

        pre_turns = TURN_SINGLE.get(direction, [])

        seq = []
        for i in range(total_repeat):
            seq.extend(pre_turns)          # turn(s) before the action
            seq.append(act)                # the primitive action
            # for an 'around' direction we need a turn after the action,
            # but that turn is also the pre‑turn of the next iteration,
            # so we add it only when another iteration follows.
            if direction.startswith("around") and i != total_repeat - 1:
                seq.extend(pre_turns)
        return seq

    def parse(s: str) -> list:
        """Recursively handle 'after' and 'and' operators."""
        s = s.strip()
        # 'after' has the lowest precedence: X after Y  →  Y then X
        if " after " in s:
            left, right = s.split(" after ", 1)
            return parse(right) + parse(left)

        # 'and' concatenates in the given order
        parts = s.split(" and ")
        result = []
        for part in parts:
            result.extend(parse_phrase(part))
        return result

    return " ".join(parse(x))

    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    The language supports the following constructs:

    * primitive actions: jump, walk, run, look, turn
    * directions: left, right
    * modifiers:
        - opposite   → turn twice in the given direction (180° turn)
        - around     → repeat the (turn + action) pattern a fixed number of times
        - twice / thrice → repeat the whole phrase 2 or 3 times
    * sequencing:
        - “and”  → left part then right part
        - “after” → left part is performed *after* the right part (i.e. right part first)

    The repeat factor for the *around* modifier is action‑specific:
        jump → 2, walk → 4, run → 9, turn → 4, look → 5
    """
    import re

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # helpers
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    around_factor = {
        "jump": 2,
        "walk": 4,
        "run": 9,
        "turn": 4,
        "look": 5,
    }

    action_token = {
        "jump": "I_JUMP",
        "walk": "I_WALK",
        "run":  "I_RUN",
        "look": "I_LOOK",
        "turn": "I_TURN",   # will be expanded with direction later
    }

    count_word = {"twice": 2, "thrice": 3}
    direction_word = {"left": "LEFT", "right": "RIGHT"}

    def tokenise(s: str):
        """split a command into lower‑case words, collapsing multiple spaces."""
        return re.findall(r"\b\w+\b", s.lower())

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # core parser – works recursively on “and” / “after”
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def parse_expr(tokens):
        """
        Parse a list of tokens that may contain the binary operators
        “and” and “after”.  Returns a flat list of primitive actions.
        """
        # handle “and” (left‑to‑right)
        if "and" in tokens:
            idx = tokens.index("and")
            left = parse_expr(tokens[:idx])
            right = parse_expr(tokens[idx + 1 :])
            return left + right

        # handle “after” (right part first)
        if "after" in tokens:
            idx = tokens.index("after")
            left = parse_expr(tokens[:idx])          # thing that happens after …
            right = parse_expr(tokens[idx + 1 :])    # … this thing
            return right + left

        # no binary operator – must be a single action phrase
        return parse_phrase(tokens)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # phrase parser – a single action with optional modifiers
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def parse_phrase(tokens):
        """
        Parse a phrase like
            “jump around left thrice”
        and return the expanded list of primitive actions.
        """
        # defaults
        cnt = 1
        around = False
        opposite = False
        direction = None

        # copy so we can pop
        t = tokens[:]

        # count words (twice / thrice) may appear anywhere – pull them out first
        for w in list(t):
            if w in count_word:
                cnt = count_word[w]
                t.remove(w)

        # modifiers “around” and “opposite”
        if "around" in t:
            around = True
            t.remove("around")
        if "opposite" in t:
            opposite = True
            t.remove("opposite")

        # direction (left / right) – may appear before or after the action word
        # we look for the first occurrence
        for w in t:
            if w in direction_word:
                direction = w
                t.remove(w)
                break

        # what remains should be the action word
        if not t:
            raise ValueError("no action found")
        action = t[0]          # jump / walk / run / look / turn
        if action not in action_token:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown action {action}")

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # compute how many times the (turn + action) pattern repeats
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        repeats = cnt
        if around:
            repeats *= around_factor[action]

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # build the token list for one repetition
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        seq = []

        # turn(s) that precede the action (except when the action itself is turn)
        if action != "turn":
            if direction:
                turn_dir = direction_word[direction]
                turn_times = 2 if opposite else 1
                seq.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_times)

        # the primitive action token itself
        if action == "turn":
            # a turn action is itself a turn token; opposite means two turns
            turn_dir = direction_word[direction] if direction else "LEFT"
            turn_times = 2 if opposite else 1
            seq.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_times)
        else:
            seq.append(action_token[action])

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # repeat the pattern the required number of times
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        result = []
        for _ in range(repeats):
            result.extend(seq)

        return result

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # entry point
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    tokens = tokenise(x)
    expanded = parse_expr(tokens)
    return " ".join(expanded)

    """
    Convert a SCAN‑style command into a space‑separated list of primitive actions.
    The language supports the following constructs:

    * primitive actions: jump, walk, run, look, turn
    * directions: left, right
    * modifiers:
        - opposite   → turn twice in the given direction (180° turn)
        - around     → repeat the (turn + action) pattern a fixed number of times
        - twice / thrice → repeat the whole phrase 2 or 3 times
    * sequencing:
        - “and”  → left part then right part
        - “after” → left part is performed *after* the right part (i.e. right part first)

    The repeat factor for the *around* modifier is action‑specific:
        jump → 2, walk → 4, run → 9, turn → 4, look → 5
    """
    import re

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # helpers
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    around_factor = {
        "jump": 2,
        "walk": 4,
        "run": 9,
        "turn": 4,
        "look": 5,
    }

    action_token = {
        "jump": "I_JUMP",
        "walk": "I_WALK",
        "run":  "I_RUN",
        "look": "I_LOOK",
        "turn": "I_TURN",   # will be expanded with direction later
    }

    count_word = {"twice": 2, "thrice": 3}
    direction_word = {"left": "LEFT", "right": "RIGHT"}

    def tokenise(s: str):
        """split a command into lower‑case words, collapsing multiple spaces."""
        return re.findall(r"\b\w+\b", s.lower())

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # core parser – works recursively on “and” / “after”
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def parse_expr(tokens):
        """
        Parse a list of tokens that may contain the binary operators
        “and” and “after”.  Returns a flat list of primitive actions.
        """
        # handle “and” (left‑to‑right)
        if "and" in tokens:
            idx = tokens.index("and")
            left = parse_expr(tokens[:idx])
            right = parse_expr(tokens[idx + 1 :])
            return left + right

        # handle “after” (right part first)
        if "after" in tokens:
            idx = tokens.index("after")
            left = parse_expr(tokens[:idx])          # thing that happens after …
            right = parse_expr(tokens[idx + 1 :])    # … this thing
            return right + left

        # no binary operator – must be a single action phrase
        return parse_phrase(tokens)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # phrase parser – a single action with optional modifiers
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def parse_phrase(tokens):
        """
        Parse a phrase like
            “jump around left thrice”
        and return the expanded list of primitive actions.
        """
        # defaults
        cnt = 1
        around = False
        opposite = False
        direction = None

        # copy so we can pop
        t = tokens[:]

        # count words (twice / thrice) may appear anywhere – pull them out first
        for w in list(t):
            if w in count_word:
                cnt = count_word[w]
                t.remove(w)

        # modifiers “around” and “opposite”
        if "around" in t:
            around = True
            t.remove("around")
        if "opposite" in t:
            opposite = True
            t.remove("opposite")

        # direction (left / right) – may appear before or after the action word
        # we look for the first occurrence
        for w in t:
            if w in direction_word:
                direction = w
                t.remove(w)
                break

        # what remains should be the action word
        if not t:
            raise ValueError("no action found")
        action = t[0]          # jump / walk / run / look / turn
        if action not in action_token:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown action {action}")

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # compute how many times the (turn + action) pattern repeats
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        repeats = cnt
        if around:
            repeats *= around_factor[action]

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # build the token list for one repetition
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        seq = []

        # turn(s) that precede the action (except when the action itself is turn)
        if action != "turn":
            if direction:
                turn_dir = direction_word[direction]
                turn_times = 2 if opposite else 1
                seq.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_times)

        # the primitive action token itself
        if action == "turn":
            # a turn action is itself a turn token; opposite means two turns
            turn_dir = direction_word[direction] if direction else "LEFT"
            turn_times = 2 if opposite else 1
            seq.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_times)
        else:
            seq.append(action_token[action])

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # repeat the pattern the required number of times
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        result = []
        for _ in range(repeats):
            result.extend(seq)

        return result

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # entry point
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    tokens = tokenise(x)
    expanded = parse_expr(tokens)
    return " ".join(expanded)

            right = parse_expr(tokens[idx + 1 :])    # … this thing
            return right + left

        # no binary operator – must be a single action phrase
        return parse_phrase(tokens)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # phrase parser – a single action with optional modifiers
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def parse_phrase(tokens):
        """
        Parse a phrase like
            “jump around left thrice”
        and return the expanded list of primitive actions.
        """
        # defaults
        cnt = 1
        around = False
        opposite = False
        direction = None

        # copy so we can pop
        t = tokens[:]

        # count words (twice / thrice) may appear anywhere – pull them out first
        for w in list(t):
            if w in count_word:
                cnt = count_word[w]
                t.remove(w)

        # modifiers “around” and “opposite”
        if "around" in t:
            around = True
            t.remove("around")
        if "opposite" in t:
            opposite = True
            t.remove("opposite")

        # direction (left / right) – may appear before or after the action word
        # we look for the first occurrence
        for w in t:
            if w in direction_word:
                direction = w
                t.remove(w)
                break

        # what remains should be the action word
        if not t:
            raise ValueError("no action found")
        action = t[0]          # jump / walk / run / look / turn
        if action not in action_token:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown action {action}")

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # compute how many times the (turn + action) pattern repeats
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        repeats = cnt
        if around:
            repeats *= around_factor[action]

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # build the token list for one repetition
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        seq = []

        # turn(s) that precede the action (except when the action itself is turn)
        if action != "turn":
            if direction:
                turn_dir = direction_word[direction]
                turn_times = 2 if opposite else 1
                seq.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_times)

        # the primitive action token itself
        if action == "turn":
            # a turn action is itself a turn token; opposite means two turns
            turn_dir = direction_word[direction] if direction else "LEFT"
            turn_times = 2 if opposite else 1
            seq.extend([f"I_TURN_{turn_dir}"] * turn_times)
        else:
            seq.append(action_token[action])

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # repeat the pattern the required number of times
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        result = []
        for _ in range(repeats):
            result.extend(seq)

        return result

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # entry point
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    tokens = tokenise(x)
    expanded = parse_expr(tokens)
    return " ".join(expanded)

    """

    """

        "run":  "I_RUN",
        "look": "I_LOOK",

    }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def parse_atom(tokens):
        # tokens – list of lower‑case words describing one action
        verb = tokens[0]                     # jump / walk / run / look / turn
        i = 1
        modifier = None                      # None / "around" / "opposite"
        direction = None

        # optional modifier
        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in ("around", "opposite"):
            modifier = tokens[i]
            i += 1

        # optional direction (look/jump etc. may be direction‑less)
        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in dirs:
            direction = tokens[i]
            i += 1

        # optional count word
        count = None
        if i < len(tokens) and tokens[i] in counts:
            count = counts[tokens[i]]
            i += 1

        # default repetition
        if count is None:
            if modifier == "around":
                count = 4                     # “around” without a number → 4 repeats
            else:
                count = 1

        actions = []

        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Build the primitive actions for the required number of repetitions
        # ------------------------------------------------------------------
        for _ in range(count):

                if modifier == "opposite":
                    actions.append(turn_token)
                    actions.append(turn_token)
                else:                         # normal or “around”
                    actions.append(turn_token)

            # 2. the primitive action itself
            actions.append(verb_action[verb])

        return actions

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Parse a possibly compound phrase (handles “and” / “after”)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    def parse_phrase(text):
        # split on top‑level “and”
        parts = [p.strip() for p in text.split(" and ")]

            # handle “after” – note that “A after B” means B first, then A

                result.extend(parse_phrase(right))

            else:

                tokens = part.split()
                result.extend(parse_atom(tokens))
        return result

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    command = command.lower().strip()
    actions = parse_phrase(command)
    return " ".join(actions)
